docs.title: RICC — Russian IT Community Corpus
docs.text: RICC (Russian IT Community Corpus) is a production-grade data engineering platform for LLM dataset curation with Zero-PII guarantees.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• End-to-end Pipeline: 7-stage data curation from raw Telegram exports to SFT/DPO/RAG datasets
  • Zero-PII Guarantees: Dual-layer scrubbing (Regex + NER) + pseudonymization + probabilistic audit
  • Deduplication: Exact hashing + MinHash LSH for fuzzy near-duplicate detection
  • Taxonomy Classification: 9 IT domains with 500+ technical keywords via Aho-Corasick
  • Conversation Graph: Thread DAG reconstruction with reply-time heuristics
  • Multi-format Export: Parquet, ShareGPT, Alpaca, OpenAI ChatML, RAG JSONL, DPO pairs
  • Analytics Engine: Deep statistical + semantic analysis with interactive reports
  • Probabilistic PII Audit: Stratified sampling + Wilson CI + power analysis (α=0.01)
  • Drift Monitoring: PSI + Jensen-Shannon + Vocabulary Jaccard with thresholds
  • SLO Gate: Fail-closed privacy, fail-open informational — SHIP/HOLD verdicts
  • LoRA Training: Multi-model batch training with typed GPU/ML error taxonomy & model zoo
  • RAG Pipeline: Hybrid lexical pre-filter + per-query TF-IDF cosine re-rank (CPU-only)
  • Observability: Structured logging (structlog) + Prometheus metrics + Grafana stack
  • Typed Exceptions: Complete error hierarchy with GPU/ML taxonomy, context & recoverability

docs.title: Installation

pip install ricc

Or with optional platform dependencies (Prefect, DVC):

pip install ricc[platform]

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from ricc import Settings, MasterDataPipeline

# Configure (or use defaults)
settings = Settings()

# Run full pipeline
pipeline = MasterDataPipeline()
summary = pipeline.run_all()

print(f"Processed {summary['cleaned_messages_count']:,} messages")
print(f"Extracted {summary['sft_dialogues_count']:,} SFT dialogues")
print(f"Validation: {'PASSED' if summary['validation_passed'] else 'FAILED'}")

docs.title: ADR 0001: Hugging Face Token Handling
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-08-29 Authors: RICC maintainers Supersedes: —

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The lora_adapters/ directory is mirrored to wwewtech/russian-it-community-lora on the Hugging Face Hub via scripts/sync_to_hub.py. The Hub requires an authentication token, which is a long-lived secret with write access to that repo.

During the 2026-08-29 audit we discovered that a real HF token was pasted into chat, and the conversation log was then summarized into a new session context. Tokens that travel through chat are considered compromised: they end up in scrollback, screen-shares, exported transcripts, and downstream context windows, and once shipped there is no reliable way to scrub them.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The HF token MUST NOT appear in:

  • Source code, comments, or docstrings
  • CLI flags or positional arguments
  • Chat, issues, pull requests, or commit messages
  • Documentation examples
  • Test fixtures

The token MUST be supplied through one of the following channels only:

  1. The HF_TOKEN environment variable (preferred for CI and one-off runs).
  2. The ~/.huggingface/token cache file (preferred for interactive use, written by huggingface-cli login).

scripts/sync_to_hub.py is the only sanctioned upload path and enforces these rules:

  • Reads HF_TOKEN from the environment first, then falls back to HfFolder.get_token().
  • Exits with code 3 if neither source provides a token.
  • Never prints the token value, even when --apply is passed.
  • Defaults to a dry-run; --apply is required for a real upload.

If a token is ever exposed through chat, logs, or commit history, it MUST be revoked at https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens and rotated before any further sync.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive:

  • Single, auditable entry point for Hub writes.
  • No accidental token leakage in screenshots, recordings, or context windows.
  • The default dry-run mode prevents accidental writes from a copy-paste or a stray shell history entry.

Negative / costs:

  • Interactive huggingface-cli login is required on each new machine; there is no shared "dev token" baked into the repo.
  • CI must use GitHub Actions secrets (HF_TOKEN is already configured there, scoped to this repo).
  • Local developers must remember to revoke any token they ever type into a chat window.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Embed the token in .env and load it via python-dotenv. Rejected: .env files are routinely pasted into chats and shown in screen-shares, so this provides only a thin layer of protection.
  • Use a per-developer token file path. Rejected: the standard ~/.huggingface/token is already supported and is the recommended Hugging Face workflow.
  • Mint a fine-grained, read-only token for the local script. Rejected: the sync script needs write access to push registry.json.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• scripts/sync_to_hub.py — the implementation that enforces this policy.
  • Hugging Face Hub authentication docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/en/quick-start#authentication

docs.title: ADR 0002: Complete mypy --strict Rollout
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-14 Authors: RICC maintainers Supersedes: —

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The codebase started with mypy in "slow mode": strict checks only for a hand-picked module list (make typecheck-strict), with [[tool.mypy.overrides]] ignore_errors masking ricc.evaluation.* and ricc.lora.* — the heaviest, most failure-prone code in the repo (GPU training, benchmark harnesses).

This was a deliberate trade-off, not an accident: transformers/peft ship weak stubs, and a big-bang strict rollout would have surfaced hundreds of errors in code nobody was ready to refactor. The cost was real, though:

  • the ignore block hid genuinely broken annotations (2 latent arg-type errors in benchmark_comparator.py were found the day the wildcard was narrowed);
  • untyped dict payloads (Collection[str] inferred where list[dict[str, Any]] was meant) produced silent runtime-shape bugs that only surfaced in GPU-time evaluation runs;
  • "strict, except these modules" drifts: modules rotted while excluded, and nobody could tell which exclusions were load-bearing.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Strict is the terminal state. Every module under ricc/ passes mypy --strict; the ignore_errors override block is removed entirely (12.2.0).
  2. The rollout is per-module, gated, and monotonic. Modules enter make typecheck-strict one at a time, only when clean. Once in, never out. History: 31 modules (2026-09-17) → 40 (2026-10-12, phase 1: ricc.lora.* + academic benchmarks, 43 errors) → 43 (2026-10-14, phase 2: the three heavy eval suites, 152 errors).
  3. cast(Any, ...) is the single sanctioned fence for untyped third-party calls (transformers/peft). Bare # type: ignore is banned on new code — it hides whole-expression errors; a cast documents the expected type and survives stub improvements.
  4. Data tables are annotated at the declaration site (HUMANEVAL_TASKS: list[dict[str, Any]] = [...]), which fixes every downstream consumer at once instead of casting each access.
  5. The gate is enforced in three places that must stay in sync: make typecheck-strict, the pre-commit mypy-strict hook (pass_filenames: false — appending staged files caused mypy "Duplicate module" errors), and the CI Typecheck (Strict) job.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• New modules must be written strict from the start and added to both lists (Makefile + pre-commit). The full recipe lives in docs/development/type-checking.md.
  • Stub fixes from transformers/peft releases can turn cast(Any, ...) calls into no-ops — casts are cheap to leave and easy to bulk-remove later; no action required.
  • Type errors are caught at PR time, not in GPU-time evaluation runs.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Rollout history and patterns: docs/development/type-checking.md
  • CHANGELOG 12.2.0, "Changed" section

docs.title: ADR 0003: Fail-Closed SLO Release Gates
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-14 Authors: RICC maintainers Supersedes: —

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
RICC publishes a dataset whose headline property is zero PII. A release decision (SHIP/HOLD) therefore has an asymmetric failure mode: a false SHIP publishes leaked personal data and cannot be undone (dumps are mirrored, cached, forked); a false HOLD merely delays a release.

Before the SLO gate, release quality was judged by eyeballing several JSON reports, each produced by a different job. That had two failure modes:

  1. Missing proof read as success. If a job was skipped or its report was never written, nothing failed — the release went out unaudited.
  2. Synthetic data could green-light a release. CI builds 100-row synthetic fixtures for speed; a gate that only checks "does the report say PASS" cannot tell a synthetic smoke run from a real corpus.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
ricc/monitoring/slo_gate.py aggregates all quality signals into one SHIP/HOLD verdict with explicit, asymmetric policy:

  1. Privacy signals fail closed. A missing probabilistic_pii_audit report or a missing/stale dataset_manifest.json is HOLD, not PASS. No proof = no release.
  2. Informational signals fail open (with a visible warning in the checks list): drift moderate_drift from sampling noise, absent sft_quality_report, absent hub_reconciliation report. Blocking on these would train maintainers to override the gate.
  3. Synthetic data can never SHIP. CI fixture runs are stamped _source.synthetic=true; the gate downgrades SHIP to HOLD with an explicit synthetic-smoke check. A deliberate override requires changing the stamp, which is reviewable.
  4. The verdict is a single artifact (reports/slo_verdict.json) with per-check passed/detail, consumed by CI, the release workflow and the RiccSloGateHold alert. No report eyeballing.
  5. Provenance is part of the gate: canonical parquet artifacts are verified against the sha256 manifest (verify_manifest, itself hardened against path escape/symlink attacks) — a release cannot ship artifacts other than the audited ones.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Release pauses are explainable: every HOLD names the failing check and the reason.
  • Adding a new quality signal means adding a check with an explicit blocking/non-blocking classification — the asymmetry decision is made once, in code, not under release pressure.
  • The drift check's "moderate is informational" policy is documented and tested (tests/test_hybrid_rag_slo.py); changing it is an ADR-level decision, not a threshold tweak.

docs.title: References
docs.text:

  • User guide: docs/user-guide/slo-gate.md
  • Manifest hardening: tests/test_artifact_manifest.py

docs.title: ADR 0004: Prometheus/Grafana Monitoring Stack
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-14 Authors: RICC maintainers Supersedes: —

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
RICC already emitted Prometheus metrics (ricc/observability) and structured logs, but the metrics went nowhere: no scrape config, no dashboards, no alerts. The failure modes this allowed:

  • Alerts without a taxonomy. "Errors went up" is not actionable; without a typed error classification, an OOM (retry with a smaller batch) and a corrupt adapter (fail fast) page identically.
  • Silent quality drift. Zero-PII is the platform's core SLO, but nothing watched it continuously — the proof existed only as CI job artifacts, reviewed manually, after the fact.
  • Guard-free dashboards. A renamed metric silently blanks a panel; dashboards rot invisibly because nothing compares them to the code.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. A typed error taxonomy is the alert vocabulary (ADR-coupled with the P3 work): MLError/GPUError hierarchy in ricc/errors.py; classify_ml_exception() maps raw torch/HF exceptions; record_classified_ml_error() records them into ricc_errors_total{component, error_type} with an allowlist (ML_COMPONENTS) that bounds label cardinality — ad-hoc components cannot inflate the series.
  2. Severity encodes the release asymmetry (mirrors ADR-0003): PII leaks and LEAKS_DETECTED verdicts are critical (page now); drift/SLO-HOLD/validation/GPU-error spikes are warning (investigate before the next release).
  3. Every metric referenced by dashboards or alerts must exist in the registry. tests/test_monitoring_stack.py parses dashboard PromQL and alert expressions and asserts each ricc_* name against prometheus_client.REGISTRY; the ServiceMonitor → Service → Deployment port chain is asserted too. Renaming a metric without updating the stack fails CI.
  4. Gauges only move on success. record_lora_result() sets loss/VRAM gauges only for successful runs — a failed run must not clobber the last known good reading; failures are counted (ricc_lora_train_total{status="failure"}) instead.
  5. Two deployment surfaces, one definition. k8s uses a ServiceMonitor + PrometheusRule CRDs (deploy/k8s/*.yaml); local Docker Compose uses an observability profile that mounts the same alert rules and provisions the same dashboard. The dashboard/definitions are never duplicated.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The Streamlit app must start the metrics server through maybe_start_metrics_server() (rerun-safe, port-conflict-safe) with RICC_METRICS_PORT — a bare start_http_server would crash on Streamlit's second rerun.
  • Alert thresholds (e.g. RiccMLComponentErrorSpike > 0.05/s) are starting points; they are versioned with the rules file and tuned by observing real runs, not silently.
  • Compose Grafana runs with an anonymous viewer for local demo use; the k8s deployment inherits cluster auth. Neither surface stores secrets.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Metric catalog + helpers: docs/api/observability.md
  • Error taxonomy: ADR context in docs/api/errors.md
  • Alert rules: deploy/k8s/prometheus-rules.yaml

docs.title: ADR 0005: A training policy gate decides what may be published
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Deciders: maintainer
  • Relates to: AGENTS.md (binding training policy), docs/user-guide/lora-training.md

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
AGENTS.md states a binding policy: a real training run must cover the whole corpus for at least one complete epoch, the acceptance criterion being actual_steps == ceil(dialogues / 8) with corpus_coverage_pct == 100.

Nothing enforced it. The consequences were concrete:

  • Seven adapters were published to the Hugging Face Hub with corpus_coverage_pct between 16.53 % and 44.62 %. They were time-boxed runs (--hours 5.8, max_steps=1000000) that stopped early.
  • 49 of the 56 published adapters had no training_meta.json at all — legacy 50-step pilot checkpoints, indistinguishable in the registry from a properly trained one.
  • The full profile itself could not satisfy the policy: its step budget was a hardcoded tier table (600–2000 steps) covering 2.77–9.24 % of the corpus, and the sample cap (12 000–20 000) truncated the dataset before the epoch could complete.
  • The coverage figure itself was wrong: it was computed as actual_steps * 8 / dataset_total, where dataset_total included the 1 000-dialogue held-out tail that is never trained on. A run covering exactly one real epoch reported 98.93 %, and the policy's own step count (21 652) was unsatisfiable alongside the holdout and eval split (one real epoch is 21 420 steps).

So the numbers in the model cards were honest, but nothing connected them to the decision "may this be published?".

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Introduce ricc/lora/policy_gate.py as the single source of truth, and call it at every point where an adapter can leave the local machine.

  1. The gate — evaluate_compliance(adapter_dir) returns a verdict with the reasons. An adapter is compliant when it has a training_meta.json, covered at least one full epoch of the trainable set, was not time-boxed, and has no missing provenance. assert_publishable() raises PolicyViolation otherwise.

  2. The step budget is derived, not hardcoded. The full profile computes the steps for one epoch from the actual dataset size (required_steps_for_epoch), so it stays correct when the corpus grows. The canonical command is produced by canonical_full_run() rather than written down in a comment.

  3. Coverage is measured against the trainable set, and the held-out tail is excluded from the denominator.

  4. The gate runs before publication — in the trainer (before the Hub upload), in finalize_sync_all.upload_missing_adapters (non-compliant adapters are skipped and logged, not uploaded) and in the registry generator (which records policy_compliant and the coverage).

  5. Partial runs are labelled, not hidden. A run stopped by a wall-clock budget is reported as PARTIAL with the reason, so an operator can see what happened instead of finding a "SUCCESS" with 16 % coverage.

  6. CI reports the compliance of the whole zoo as reports/lora_policy_compliance.json. It does not fail the build on the legacy adapters — that would require retraining them, which is a GPU job, not a code change — but the state is visible and the release pipeline enforces it.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A non-compliant adapter can no longer reach the Hub through any of the three publication paths, and the registry says which adapters are publishable.
  • The currently published zoo is entirely non-compliant (0 of 56). The adapters that are already on the Hub stay there until they are retrained; this ADR does not retroactively unpublish them, and the model cards state the real coverage.
  • The canonical full run is expensive by design: ~25 h on a 3B model, ~13 h on 1.5B, ~5–7 h below 1B on the RTX 3060. A "fast" run is possible, but it is a smoke test and says so.

docs.title: Alternatives rejected
docs.text:
• Keep the policy in AGENTS.md only. It was already there and was already ignored. A policy without an enforcement point is a comment.
  • Delete the non-compliant adapters. They are useful as smoke artefacts and as evidence that the pipeline works; hiding them would make the problem invisible rather than solved.
  • Publish with a warning. A published adapter is downloaded and used by people; the warning is read by nobody. Refusing to publish is the only effective line.

docs.title: ADR 0006: The published dataset contract is declared, versioned and enforced
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Deciders: maintainer
  • Relates to: docs/architecture/data-models.md, ricc/validation/validator.py

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The public contract of this project is the column set of the exported Parquet files. A consumer who downloads full_clean_messages.parquet and writes code against text_clean, domain and tags needs to know when one of those is renamed, removed or retyped.

Nothing carried that information:

  • ricc/validation/artifact_manifest.py had SCHEMA_VERSION = 1, but that versions the manifest format, not the data — a reader of the code could reasonably think otherwise.
  • DatasetValidator.validate_parquet_files claimed to check "schema conformance" but only counted columns (col_count = table.num_columns) and compared nothing. A renamed column, a reordered column or a retyped column all passed silently.
  • The Parquet files carried only the pandas metadata block, so nothing in a downloaded file said which contract it was written against.

docs/architecture/data-models.md promised "dtypes pinned by DatasetValidator", which was not true.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Declare the contract in code, version it, write it into the artefacts and enforce it.

  1. ricc/schema_version.py is the declaration. It lists, for every exported artefact, the column names, their order and their Arrow types. The values were taken from the published files and are verified against them by a test, so the declaration cannot drift away from the data unnoticed.

  2. A version and a fingerprint. DATASET_SCHEMA_VERSION is semver: MAJOR when a column is removed or retyped (a breaking change for a consumer), MINOR when a column is added, PATCH for documentation. The schema_fingerprint() hashes the whole contract, so a change to any column of any artefact is detectable even when the version was not bumped.

  3. The version travels with the data. The exporter writes the version and the fingerprint into the Parquet key-value metadata, next to the existing pandas block, so a downloaded file says which contract it was written against.

  4. The validator enforces it. The column names, their order and their types must match the declaration, and the version metadata must be present and current. A mismatch fails the validation with the status INVALID and a list of the problems — it is not logged and ignored.

  5. A machine-readable manifest. reports/dataset_schema.json records the version, the fingerprint and the full contract. It is generated by scripts/generate_schema_manifest.py (with a --check mode wired into CI) and is derived from the code, never hand-maintained.

docs.title: Why the JSONL exports are versioned differently
docs.text: The JSONL exports are declared in the contract as well, with their record shape, but their version travels in the contract manifest rather than in the files. A header line would be the natural in-band choice, but the JSONL validator counts valid lines, and the consumers rely on "every line is a record". A header would break that contract for every downstream reader. The sidecar manifest carries the same information without touching the data files.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A consumer can verify what they downloaded: the fingerprint in the file must match the one in the manifest for the release they expect.
  • A column rename is now a validation failure, not a silent change that surfaces weeks later in somebody's notebook.
  • The published files on the Hub predate the versioning, so they carry no version metadata and the validator reports that gap. They are correct against the declared contract (names, order and types) — only the metadata is missing. Re-exporting them adds it.
  • Adding a column is a MINOR bump and does not break a consumer that ignores it; removing or retyping one is MAJOR and must be called out in the changelog.

docs.title: Alternatives rejected
docs.text:
• Rely on the file name. The names already carry the version (sft_dialogues.parquet), but a name cannot describe a column set.
  • Version only the manifest. The manifest is downloaded separately from the data, so the pairing between "this file" and "this contract" would rely on the consumer doing the bookkeeping.
  • A separate schema.json next to every Parquet file. More files to keep in sync, and the metadata is already the place Arrow keeps file-level information.

docs.title: ADR 0007: The export streams, and DVC is a real pipeline
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Deciders: maintainer
  • Relates to: docs/development/dvc-pipeline.md, ricc/exporter/parquet_exporter.py

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Two independent parts of the platform did not do what they claimed.

docs.title: The export
docs.text:
ParquetExporter built a list of every record, a pandas.DataFrame on top of it, and wrote the result with a single to_parquet call. For the published corpus (2 816 434 messages) that is:

  • a peak memory footprint that grows with the corpus (the records list alone is ~1.24 GB for the text column, plus the DataFrame on top);
  • a file with three row groups of ~1M rows each — a reader cannot fetch a slice, it decompresses a third of the corpus.

The MinHash LSH index had the same shape: a Python list[int] of 128 entries per message, ~5 kB each, about 8.9 GB for the 1.78M indexed messages of the corpus.

docs.title: DVC
docs.text:
dvc.yaml described twelve stages, params.yaml was called "the single source of truth", and make dvc-repro was documented. None of it worked:

  • dvc init had never been run: there was no .dvc/, no dvc.lock and no remote;
  • the stages were inline python -c "..." blocks, which do not survive a Windows shell — cmd.exe splits the multi-line quoted string and the stage dies with 'from' is not recognized as an internal or external command. So dvc repro had never run, on any platform;
  • the ingest stage declared only source files as dependencies, never the raw Telegram exports, so DVC could not detect a change in the corpus;
  • pii_audit.sample_size was declared as a parameter of three stages that do not use it, so editing it invalidated unrelated stages — and the value was not read anywhere at runtime either (see ADR 0008);
  • the drift stage compared the corpus against itself, so it could only ever report "stable".

docs.title: The export streams
docs.text:
write_records_streaming writes through a pyarrow.parquet.ParquetWriter in batches. The consequences:

  • the peak memory is bounded by the row group, not by the corpus. With a 10k row group the peak stays flat at ~36 MB for 20k, 80k and 320k records alike, where the old path grew linearly (102 MB at 100k rows, 1.6 GB at 1.6M rows);
  • the file has 29 row groups instead of 3, so a consumer can read a slice;
  • the schema is pinned (MESSAGE_SCHEMA / SFT_SCHEMA / RAG_SCHEMA), because inferring it from the first batch alone is unsafe: a first batch whose reply_to_id is all-None yields a null column and a later batch with real integers then fails outright;
  • the write is atomic (.partial + os.replace), so a failed export can never leave a truncated file where a consumer expects a dataset;
  • the file grows ~7 % (198.5 → 212.6 MB): zstd compresses a large block better than a small one. The extra bytes buy the ability to read a slice.

The MinHash signatures moved into one contiguous uint32 block: 8.9 GB → 0.9 GB for the corpus, and the permutation arithmetic is vectorised over the shingles, so the index is also faster.

docs.title: The pipeline stages stream too
docs.text:
The export was only the last stage. The stages before it held the input list AND the output list at the same time:

  • the PII stage built a list of every NormalizedMessage, then a list of every CleanedMessage;
  • the deduplication stage built a second list of the survivors on top;
  • the MinHash index added its own signatures.

At 2.8M messages that is several gigabytes of live objects that exist only because a list needs to be a list. Each stage now has a streaming variant that takes an ITERABLE and yields its result:

  • UnifiedPIIAnonymizer.process_stream — the author pass still reads the whole corpus (the inflected name forms have to be known before any text is scrubbed, and only a few thousand author identities are kept), then the scrubbing yields one message at a time;
  • ExactDeduplicator.deduplicate_stream — the fingerprints are stored as raw 8-byte digests instead of 32-character hex strings;
  • MinHashLSH.deduplicate_stream — the index is the signature block.

MasterDataPipeline.run_all() uses the streaming variants and releases the raw messages as soon as the PII stage is done, so the deduplication stage never sees them.

The list-based methods (process_batch, deduplicate, deduplicate_messages) still exist and behave identically — the streaming variants are the same code with a different boundary.

docs.title: DVC is real
docs.text:
• dvc init has been run; .dvc/config names a remote and dvc.lock is committed;
  • every stage is a real script (scripts/dvc_stages.py <stage>) with a main(), invocable by DVC or by hand and unit-testable;
  • the raw exports are a declared dependency of the ingest stage. DVC does not expand globs in deps:, so they are listed explicitly and scripts/refresh_dvc_deps.py --check keeps the list in sync;
  • a parameter is declared only by the stage that reads it;
  • the drift stage compares against a frozen reference snapshot (RICC_DRIFT_REFERENCE), never against the current file;
  • CI has a job that checks the dependency list, the stage definitions (no inline python -c) and the lock file.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Exporting the corpus no longer needs a machine with tens of gigabytes of free RAM for the export step alone, and the same is now true of the PII and deduplication stages.
  • The published files on the Hub still have three row groups; they will be re-exported with the streaming writer, which changes their bytes and therefore their manifest hashes. The dataset version is unchanged (the contract is the same), but the artefact hashes are.
  • The DVC pipeline now has a real cost: dvc repro on the full corpus runs the whole pipeline, which is hours of GPU-free CPU work plus the MinHash pass. The lock file and the cache make the second run cheap.
  • The DVC remote defaults to a local directory outside the working copy. A shared setup points it at object storage; the rest of the configuration does not change.
  • The PII stage still needs two passes over the corpus: the inflected forms of a name are only known once the name has been seen, so the author pass runs before the scrubbing pass. That is inherent to the algorithm, not to the streaming — and it costs a few thousand author identities, not a second copy of the corpus.

docs.title: Alternatives rejected
docs.text:
• Keep the list-and-DataFrame export. It works on a small corpus and fails exactly where it matters.
  • Use row_group_size on the existing call. That fixes the file layout but not the memory: the whole corpus is still materialised twice before the write.
  • Delete the DVC layer. Tempting — it did not work. But the pipeline description is the reproducibility contract of a data project, and deleting it would leave the corpus with no way to be rebuilt from the raw exports. Fixing it was cheaper than replacing it.

docs.title: ADR 0008: One live configuration object, no frozen snapshots
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Deciders: maintainer
  • Relates to: ricc/settings.py, docs/architecture/overview.md

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The project had two configuration sources, and the second one was a trap.

ricc/settings.py held the real configuration: a pydantic-settings Settings instance loaded from the environment (the RICC__ prefix) and from params.yaml. Every field is derived from a base field through a read-only property (parquet_output_dir → PARQUET_OUTPUT_DIR).

ricc/config.py re-exported the same values as a snapshot taken at import time:

OUTPUT_DIR = settings.OUTPUT_DIR
MINHASH_NUM_PERM = settings.MINHASH_NUM_PERM

ricc/pipeline.py carried six more of the same constants, with a comment that said it plainly: "Backward compatibility for tests that patch these module-level constants". The tests were dictating the architecture: the production code held a second, frozen copy of the configuration so that the tests could patch it.

The consequence was measured, not theoretical:

config.OUTPUT_DIR (snapshot)          : ...\dataset_output
Settings(output_dir=...).OUTPUT_DIR   : \tmp\custom-output

A consumer that built its own Settings — the documented way to configure the library — got a different configuration than every module that had imported the shim. An environment variable set after the import was ignored by the shim and honoured by the live object.

Two copies of the same configuration is also a drift hazard: the earlier history of this project had ~520 duplicated lines (the path constants, the MinHash tuning, the sentiment lexicon, the stopwords and the full 8-domain taxonomy) between config.py and settings.py, at 79 % textual similarity. The shim was the last remnant of that.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
There is one configuration object, and it is read live.

  1. ricc/config.py is removed. The compatibility argument for it died with the src. → ricc. rename: every consumer is in this repository.
  2. ricc/pipeline.py no longer holds module-level copies. The exporters, the scripts and the CLI read settings.<FIELD> at the point of use.
  3. ricc/monitoring/slo_gate.py takes the reports directory as an argument that defaults to the live settings.REPORTS_DIR.
  4. The tests patch the underlying pydantic fields (ricc.settings.settings.output_dir), not the derived properties (which are read-only) and not module constants.

ricc/settings.py stays the single source; params.yaml is the runtime source of the nested sections and the domain taxonomy.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A consumer's own Settings instance is now honoured everywhere.
  • There is one place to change a default, and one place to read it.
  • The ricc/config.py import path is gone. It was an internal module of a library that was never published under that name (the wheel was broken until 2026-10-21), so there is no public API break.
  • The tests no longer need the production code to carry a second copy of the configuration. A test asserts that no module holds a module-level copy of a settings value, so the pattern cannot come back.

docs.title: Alternatives rejected
docs.text:
• Keep the shim, but make it lazy. A module-level __getattr__ would forward to settings, so the snapshot problem would go. But a module whose whole purpose is to forward names adds an indirection and a second import path for the same values; removing it is simpler and the compatibility cost is zero.
  • Make Settings mutable and patch it in tests. Pydantic models are validated on assignment, and a mutable global configuration is exactly what caused the original drift. The read-only properties over base fields give the tests a clean seam without that.

docs.title: Errors — Typed Exception Hierarchy
docs.text:
All RICC exceptions derive from RICCError and carry structured context (component, context dict, recoverable flag) so failures can be logged, counted in Prometheus, and acted on programmatically.

from ricc.errors import GPUOutOfMemoryError, classify_ml_exception, RICCError

RICCError
├── PipelineError            (stage-tagged: ingestion, deduplication, ...)
│   ├── IngestionError
│   ├── PIIAnonymizationError
│   ├── DeduplicationError
│   ├── TaxonomyError
│   ├── GraphExtractionError
│   ├── ExportError
│   └── AnalyticsError
├── ValidationError          (check-tagged: schema, pii_audit, sft, jsonl, parquet, slo)
│   ├── SchemaValidationError
│   ├── PIIValidationError
│   ├── SFTValidationError
│   ├── JSONLValidationError
│   ├── ParquetValidationError

docs.title: GPU / ML Taxonomy (P3)
docs.text: Added in 12.2.0. Motivation: LoRA training and eval harnesses previously raised bare RuntimeError or let torch exceptions propagate, making it impossible to distinguish "retry with a smaller batch" (OOM) from "fail fast — weights are corrupt" (adapter load) in logs and alerts.

docs.title: MLError — training / inference failures
docs.text:
Class component Extra context MLError ml model_name, adapter_id TrainingError training step, phase InferenceError inference — EvaluationError evaluation benchmark, variant TokenizerError tokenizer — CheckpointError checkpoint checkpoint_path AdapterLoadError adapter adapter_path, base_model QuantizationError quantization quant_type

AdapterLoadError must fail fast: silently falling back to the base model produces misleading "attached" metrics (see ricc/inference.py).

docs.title: GPUError — device failures
docs.text:
Class Raised when GPUNotAvailableError CUDA requested (device_map="auto", fp16) but no GPU is visible GPUDriverError driver / cuBLAS / NCCL / NVML init failures GPUOutOfMemoryError VRAM exhausted; subclass of ResourceError, so it also carries resource_type="vram", current_usage (requested MB), limit (available MB)

VRAMExhaustedError is kept as a legacy alias of GPUOutOfMemoryError — existing code and dashboards keep working.

docs.title: Classifying Raw Exceptions
docs.text:
Train/eval scripts wrap broad except blocks with classify_ml_exception, which pattern-matches OOM, CUDA-unavailable and driver errors and returns the typed exception with the original chained into context:

from ricc.errors import classify_ml_exception

try:
    trainer.train()
except Exception as exc:
    typed = classify_ml_exception(exc, model_name=model_name, adapter_id=adapter_id)
    logger.error(f"training failed: {typed}")
    raise
  • OOM (torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError or "CUDA out of memory" in message) → GPUOutOfMemoryError — retryable: smaller batch, gradient checkpointing, 4-bit quantization.
  • "no CUDA" / "device not found" → GPUNotAvailableError.
  • cuBLAS / NCCL / NVML markers → GPUDriverError.
  • Anything else → TrainingError with original_error in context.

is_oom_error(exc) is the standalone predicate.

docs.title: Recording Errors into Prometheus
docs.text:
ricc/observability.record_classified_ml_error() combines classification and recording in one call (used by all train/eval entry points):

from ricc.observability import record_classified_ml_error

except Exception as exc:
    typed = record_classified_ml_error(exc, model_name=..., adapter_id=...)
    raise

It increments ricc_errors_total{component, error_type}; component is validated against the ML_COMPONENTS allowlist, so untyped exceptions cannot inflate label cardinality. The Grafana panel "Errors by component" and the RiccMLComponentErrorSpike alert consume this series.

docs.title: Full Public API
docs.text: Import everything from the package root — ricc/ricc/__init__.py re-exports the whole hierarchy plus the Result type (Ok/Err) used for functional error handling in pipeline stages.

docs.title: Recording Helpers
docs.text:
from ricc.observability import (
    record_stage_messages,  # (stage, count)
    record_pii_leak,  # (category, count=1)
    record_validation,  # (check, passed)
    record_slo_check,  # (check, passed)
    record_error,  # (component, error_type)
    record_ml_error,  # (typed_error) -> component
    record_classified_ml_error,  # (raw_exc, **ctx) -> typed RICCError
    record_lora_result,  # (model=, adapter=, status=, duration_sec=, loss=, steps=, vram_bytes=)

)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Unified configuration via pydantic-settings.BaseSettings.

from ricc import Settings, settings

# Global instance (loads from .env + params.yaml)
settings.BASE_DIR
settings.PARQUET_OUTPUT_DIR
settings.MINHASH_NUM_PERM
settings.DOMAIN_TAXONOMY

# The nested parameter sections come from params.yaml
settings.pii_audit.sample_size  # 100000
settings.pii_audit.confidence  # 0.99
settings.pii_audit.max_leak_tolerance  # 1e-4
settings.drift.psi_stable
settings.benchmarks.humaneval_tasks

custom = Settings(minhash_num_perm=256, pii_audit=PIIAuditSettings(sample_size=100000))

params.yaml is the single source of these values — they are read at boot, so editing it changes the runtime behaviour (the audit, the drift thresholds, the benchmark sizes) without a code edit.

docs.title: MasterDataPipeline
docs.text:
End-to-end data curation pipeline.

from ricc import MasterDataPipeline

pipeline = MasterDataPipeline(raw_export_dirs=[...])
summary = pipeline.run_all()

Stages: 1. ingestion — Load & merge Telegram exports 2. pii_anonymization — Regex + NER scrubbing + pseudonymization 3. deduplication — Exact + MinHash LSH 4. taxonomy_tagging — Domain classification + keyword tagging 3. graph_extraction — Thread DAG + SFT/DPO/RAG extraction 4. export — Parquet + JSONL (ShareGPT, Alpaca, ChatML, RAG, DPO) 5. analytics_validation — Deep analytics + validation + PII audit

docs.text:
• author_* fields never contain raw usernames/ids — pseudonymization is a schema-level guarantee (the manifest pins it).
  • domain is always non-empty (falls back to general_tech_chat).
  • Parquet dtypes are pinned by DatasetValidator; a mismatch fails make validate before any release gate sees the data.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: RICC follows a 7-stage pipeline architecture with clear separation of concerns, typed interfaces, and observability built-in.

docs.title: Pipeline Stages
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Raw Telegram Exports] --> B[Ingestion]
    B --> C[PII Anonymization]
    C --> D[Deduplication]
    D --> E[Taxonomy Tagging]
    E --> F[Graph Extraction]
    F --> G[Export]
    G --> H[Analytics & Validation]
Stage Module Input Output 1. Ingestion ricc.ingestion.loader JSON exports NormalizedMessage[] 2. PII Anonymization ricc.pii.deep_anonymizer NormalizedMessage[] CleanedMessage[] 3. Deduplication ricc.deduplication.* CleanedMessage[] CleanedMessage[] (deduped) 4. Taxonomy Tagging ricc.taxonomy.tagger CleanedMessage[] CleanedMessage[] (tagged) 5. Graph Extraction ricc.graph.* CleanedMessage[] SFTDialogue[], RAGChunk[], DPOPair[] 6. Export ricc.exporter.* Datasets Parquet + JSONL 7. Analytics/Validation ricc.analytics.*, ricc.validation.* Artifacts Reports + SLO verdict

docs.title: 1. Type Safety
docs.text:
• All data models use Pydantic v2 (ricc/ingestion/schema.py)
  • mypy --strict on 31+ modules
  • Result[T, E] for functional error handling

docs.title: 2. Single Source of Truth
docs.text:
• Configuration: ricc/settings.py (pydantic-settings)
  • Pipeline params: params.yaml (DVC)
  • No hardcoded values in business logic

docs.title: 3. Observability First
docs.text:
• Structured logging via structlog (JSON)
  • Prometheus metrics on every stage
  • SLO gate with SHIP/HOLD verdicts

docs.title: 4. Graceful Degradation
docs.text:
• Prefect orchestration optional (try/except ImportError)
  • DVC optional (filesystem fallback)
  • GPU training optional (CPU fallback)

docs.title: 5. Security by Default
docs.text:
• Zero-PII design (fail-closed)
  • Read-only Docker containers
  • No secrets in code (.env.example template)
  • Artifact integrity via SHA256 manifests

docs.title: Pipeline Stages
docs.text: MasterDataPipeline (ricc/pipeline.py) runs seven stages in sequence. Each stage is wrapped in time_stage(), so its duration lands in the ricc_pipeline_stage_duration_seconds histogram and its outcome in ricc_pipeline_stage_total{stage, status}.

docs.title: Stage Diagram
docs.text:
ChatExport_*/result.json
        │
        ▼
[1] Ingestion ─── merge_multiple_exports() ──> list[NormalizedMessage]
        ▼
[2] PII anonymization ── UnifiedPIIAnonymizer ──> list[CleanedMessage]
        ▼
[3] Deduplication ── ExactDeduplicator + MinHashLSH
        ▼
[4] Taxonomy tagging ── TechnicalTagger ──> domain + tags
        ▼
[5] Graph extraction ── ThreadDAGBuilder + ConversationExtractor
        │                 ├──> list[SFTDialogue]
        │                 └──> list[RAGChunk]
        ▼

dataset_output/ + reports/

docs.title: Stage Contracts
docs.text:
Stage Input → Output Failure mode 1 Ingestion raw exports → NormalizedMessage IngestionError on unreadable/malformed export 2 PII raw text → masked text + anon ids PIIAnonymizationError 3 Dedup messages → deduplicated DeduplicationError 4 Taxonomy text → domain/tags TaxonomyError 5 Graph messages → threads/dialogues/chunks GraphExtractionError 6 Export objects → parquet/jsonl ExportError 7 Analytics artifacts → reports AnalyticsError

Typed errors carry stage context — see Errors.

docs.title: Idempotence & State
docs.text: The pipeline is stateless between runs: every run rebuilds from the raw exports. Partial artifacts from a crashed run are overwritten; the artifact manifest must be re-created after any successful run (python -m ricc.validation.artifact_manifest create ...) so the SLO gate can verify provenance.

docs.title: Runtime Environment
docs.text: ricc/bootstrap.setup_runtime_env() centralizes UTF-8 stdio (Windows cp1251 protection), HF_HOME → repo-local .hf_cache, tokenizers env and structlog configuration. Entry points call it before importing heavy third-party libraries — keep that ordering in new scripts.

docs.title: run
docs.text:
python cli.py run [--skip-ner]

Executes MasterDataPipeline.run_all(). --skip-ner replaces the Natasha NER layer with regex-only scrubbing (fast, weaker on names). Prometheus stage counters increment on every stage (ricc_pipeline_stage_total).

docs.title: analyze
docs.text:
python cli.py analyze [--limit N]

Loads full_clean_messages.parquet, runs DeepChatAnalyzer; --limit bounds the NLP-lemmatization sample (default 100000). Writes reports/analytics_summary.json.

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
python cli.py validate

DatasetValidator.validate_all() over the three canonical parquet artifacts; writes reports/validation_results.json. Non-zero exit on failure.

docs.title: benchmark
docs.text:
python cli.py benchmark

Exports the 100-question domain benchmark to reports/domain_benchmark_100.json and prints the preview table.

docs.title: audit-prob
docs.text:
python cli.py audit-prob [--parquet PATH] [--sample-size N]
                         [--confidence F] [--tolerance F] [--output PATH]

Stratified probabilistic PII audit with Wilson CI bounds (defaults: 50000 sample, 0.99 confidence, 1e-4 tolerance). Writes the report and exits non-zero when the verdict is LEAKS_DETECTED.

docs.title: drift
docs.text:
python cli.py drift [--reference PATH] [--current PATH] [--output PATH]

Defaults to a self-comparison baseline (stable). With two frozen snapshots produces real temporal drift. Writes reports/drift_report.json and records the drift gauges.

docs.title: orchestrate
docs.text:
python cli.py orchestrate [--skip-pipeline] [--sample-size N]

Runs the Prefect flow; without Prefect installed it degrades to sequential execution with a warning.

docs.title: chat
docs.text:
python cli.py chat [--model ID] [--adapter ID] [--no-rag]

Interactive session: loads model + optional LoRA adapter (validate_adapter_path fails fast on corrupt weights with AdapterLoadError) and RAG context injection. Exit commands: exit, quit, q.

docs.title: rag
docs.text:
python cli.py rag QUERY [--top-k N]

One-shot hybrid search over the knowledge base; prints title, domain, score and content per hit.

docs.title: CLI Overview
docs.text:
cli.py (installed as it-pipeline) is the operational entry point. Heavy dependencies are imported lazily per subcommand, so --help starts instantly.

make run|analyze|validate|audit|audit-prob|drift|slo|orchestrate|test|lint|format|typecheck-strict|security|reports|reports-real|ui — see make help.

Every command runs setup_runtime_env() first: UTF-8 stdio, HF cache, structured JSON logging.

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text: Workflow: .github/workflows/ci.yml — "Data Platform CI & Validation". Triggers: push/PR to main/master, workflow_dispatch, release published. Runners: pinned ubuntu-24.04.

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text:
Job What it does Notes Lint & Format ruff check + ruff format --check pinned ruff==0.16.2 Typecheck (Strict) make typecheck-strict 43 modules, mypy==2.3.1 Unit Tests pytest + coverage, matrix 3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14 --cov-fail-under=85, coverage.xml artifact Data Validation & Audits lock check, adapter cards, synthetic fixtures, validator, real-corpus PII audit (100k sample) synthetic run is stamped, never SHIP SLO Release Gate (Real Corpus) regenerates reports from real artifacts, runs the gate artifact slo_verdict.json Security Supply Chain bandit HIGH gate (0 allowed) + detect-secrets baseline + pip-audit hard gate (0 CVEs) reports as artifacts, 30d HF Token & Cache Check HF_TOKEN presence + cache layout push/dispatch only SLO Release Gate gate verdict from job-local reports release path Docker Build & Push builds ricc-data-platform, pushes on main GHCR Release to Hugging Face Hub finalize/sync/catalog on release contents: write LoRA zoo publish gh release upload of the catalog --clobber

Typical full run: 15–18 minutes. All 11 jobs green is the merge bar.

docs.title: Pinning Policy
docs.text:
• Action versions are pinned by major (actions/checkout@v5, setup-python@v6, upload-artifact@v7) and bumped by dedicated dependency PRs.
  • Tool versions are pinned exactly in pyproject.toml [dev] + MYPY_VERSION/RUFF_VERSION env so local == hook == CI.

docs.title: Security Gates
docs.text:
• bandit: HIGH severity fails the job; the full JSON report is uploaded for triage. Current baseline: 0 HIGH.
  • detect-secrets: fails on findings not in .secrets.baseline (UTF-8, regenerated 2026-10-11); baseline guarded by tests/test_secrets_baseline.py.
  • pip-audit: hard gate since 12.2.0 — any known CVE in the requirements tree fails; missing report fails closed.

docs.title: Docs Gate
docs.text: mkdocs build --strict runs in CI (docs job): every nav entry must resolve and the build must be warning-free.

docs.title: Release Flow
docs.text: release: published → SLO gate on real corpus → Docker push → Hub sync (scripts/sync_to_hub.py --apply, sanctioned token path per docs/adr/0001-hf-token-handling.md) → gh release upload the model zoo catalog.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/wwewtech/russian-it-community-corpus.git
cd russian-it-community-corpus
python -m venv .venv && .venv\Scripts\activate   # Windows
make install          # editable install + dev tools
pre-commit install    # hooks: ruff, mypy-strict, detect-secrets, yaml/toml checks

docs.title: Daily Loop
docs.text:
make lint       # ruff check (same pinned version as CI)
make format     # ruff format
make typecheck-strict   # mypy --strict over all 43 src modules
make test       # pytest with coverage gate

All four must pass locally before pushing — CI runs the same pinned versions (ruff==0.16.2, mypy==2.3.1).

docs.title: Rules of the Codebase
docs.text:
1. Strict typing is mandatory. New modules go into both strict lists (Makefile + pre-commit hook). See Type Checking for the cast(Any, ...) pattern.
  2. Single formatter: ruff format. (The Black fallback hook was removed — it disagreed with ruff and blocked commits.)
  3. No bare # type: ignore on new code.
  4. Errors are typed. Raise from ricc.errors hierarchy; raw torch/HF exceptions in train/eval entry points go through record_classified_ml_error().
  5. Metrics are deliberate. A new metric name must be added to the observability module — the guard tests fail if dashboards/rules reference unregistered names.
  6. Security gates are hard. bandit HIGH = 0, pip-audit = 0 vulnerable packages, detect-secrets = no new findings. A new HIGH finding blocks merge; fix or (with justification) add a scoped # nosec with the bare-code rule.
  7. Docs build in CI (mkdocs build --strict): every nav entry must resolve.

docs.title: Commits
docs.text: Conventional, scope-tagged: feat(2-4): ..., sec(5): ..., fix(release): ..., types(2-final): .... Version bumps touch all four places — pyproject.toml, CITATION.cff, ricc/__init__.py, ricc/ricc/__init__.py — enforced by test_version_consistency.

docs.text:

  • Tests: add for every behavior change; coverage gate is 85% with GPU-only suites omitted from the gate.
  • Update CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased → version at release time) and the relevant docs pages.

docs.title: DVC Pipeline
docs.text:
DVC (optional extra: pip install .[platform]) version-controls the data pipeline stages and the parameters that drive them.

make dvc-repro      # = dvc repro
dvc status
dvc dag

This pipeline actually runs. It did not until 2026-10-21: the stages were inline python -c "..." blocks, which do not survive a Windows shell (cmd.exe splits the multi-line quoted string and the stage dies with 'from' is not recognized as an internal or external command), and dvc init had never been executed. Every stage is now a real script, and dvc repro ingest ingests the 2 911 754 raw messages and writes dvc.lock. See ADR 0007.

docs.title: The stages
docs.text:
Stage Script Output ingest scripts/dvc_stages.py ingest dataset_output/intermediate/raw_messages.pkl.gz pii_anonymize ... pii_anonymize cleaned_messages.pkl.gz exact_dedup ... exact_dedup dedup_exact.pkl.gz minhash_dedup ... minhash_dedup dedup_minhash.pkl.gz taxonomy ... taxonomy tagged_messages.pkl.gz graph ... graph threaded_messages.pkl.gz extract ... extract extracted.pkl.gz export ... export the parquet and JSONL artefacts analytics ... analytics reports/analytics_summary.json validate ... validate the validation and PII audit reports drift ... drift reports/drift_report.json slo ... slo reports/slo_verdict.json

Each stage is invocable on its own:

python scripts/dvc_stages.py export

docs.title: The raw exports are a real dependency
docs.text:
DVC does not expand globs in a deps: entry — ChatExport_*/result.json would be recorded literally and then reported as a deleted dependency. The ingest stage therefore lists every export explicitly, and scripts/refresh_dvc_deps.py keeps the list in sync:

python scripts/refresh_dvc_deps.py           # refresh the list
python scripts/refresh_dvc_deps.py --check   # CI: fail if out of sync

The exports are gitignored (they are data, not source) and tracked by DVC, so a change in the corpus re-runs the ingestion.

docs.title: Params Contract
docs.text:
params.yaml is the single source of truth, consumed through settings (loaded at boot) and by the stages that need them:

pii_audit:      # sample_size, confidence, max_leak_tolerance
drift:          # psi/js/vocab thresholds, buckets, top_k
benchmarks:     # humaneval_tasks, rummlu_questions, confidence
domain_taxonomy: # 8 domains × keyword lists

A parameter is declared in dvc.yaml only by the stage that reads it, so editing a threshold re-runs exactly the stage it affects. The values themselves are read at runtime — settings.pii_audit and settings.benchmarks used to be dead configuration duplicated as literals in the code, the CLI and the Prefect flow, so editing params.yaml changed nothing at runtime.

docs.title: The drift stage needs a frozen reference
docs.text:
The drift stage compares the current corpus against a frozen snapshot, never against itself (comparing the corpus with itself can only ever report "stable"):

RICC_DRIFT_REFERENCE=dataset_output/parquet/full_clean_messages_reference.parquet \
    dvc repro drift

Without a reference the stage says so and skips, rather than producing a meaningless "stable" verdict.

docs.title: Remote storage
docs.text:
The default remote is a local directory outside the working copy:

dvc remote add -d storage ../ricc-dvc-storage
dvc push

For a shared setup point it at object storage instead — the rest of the configuration does not change:

dvc remote add -d s3remote s3://my-bucket/ricc

docs.title: Datasets on the Hub
docs.text: The published dataset lives at huggingface.co/datasets/wwewtech/russian-it-community-corpus; the pinned revision snapshot is reports/pinned_hub_manifest.json, and ricc/validation/hub_reconciliation.py reconciles local artifacts against it (status feeds the SLO gate).

docs.title: When to Use DVC vs the Plain Pipeline
docs.text:
• dvc repro is for parameterized, cacheable reruns of the pipeline stages; the lock file records every hash.
  • make run remains the canonical full-pipeline path (it rebuilds from raw exports; the raw exports are the source of truth).
  • CI does not require DVC for the validation jobs — they build synthetic fixtures and run the real-corpus audits directly — but there is a dvc-consistency job that checks the pipeline definition, the dependency list and the lock file agree.

make test       # pytest -q

docs.text:
• Prefer pure-function tests around the module's public API; mock only third-party boundaries (peft.PeftModel.from_pretrained, torch CUDA).
  • Every new Prometheus metric must be asserted through prometheus_client.REGISTRY in a guard test so renames fail loudly.

docs.title: Type Checking — mypy --strict Everywhere
docs.text: As of 12.2.0 the strict rollout is complete: every module under ricc/ passes mypy --strict, and the [[tool.mypy.overrides]] ignore_errors block in pyproject.toml is gone.

docs.title: Gates
docs.text:
Gate Command Modules Local / CI make typecheck-strict 43 Pre-commit mypy-strict hook (.pre-commit-config.yaml) 43 (same list) CI job Typecheck (Strict) → make typecheck-strict 43

The Makefile list and the pre-commit hook list must stay in sync — both mirror the full ricc/ module set.

docs.title: The cast(Any, ...) Pattern
docs.text:
Heavy ML libraries (transformers, peft) ship incomplete or untyped stubs; calling e.g. AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained() under --strict fails with no-untyped-call. The single sanctioned pattern (established in ricc/inference.py, used everywhere since):

from typing import Any, cast

tokenizer: Any = cast(Any, AutoTokenizer).from_pretrained(model_name, use_fast=True)
text: str = cast(str, tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))

Rules:

  • cast(Any, ...) fences the call; the result is annotated with the concrete type you expect (Any, str, dict[str, Any]).
  • Never write # type: ignore — a bare ignore hides errors in the whole expression. (Pre-existing type: ignore[misc] in ricc/orchestration/prefect_flow.py predates the policy.)
  • Prefer annotating data tables at the declaration site (HUMANEVAL_TASKS: list[dict[str, Any]] = [...]) — this fixes the type of every downstream consumer at once, instead of casting each access.

docs.title: Dict Payloads and Fallback Branches
docs.text:
When a function branches and the fallback branch reads values from a dict[str, Any] accumulator (which mypy sees as object), annotate the locals up front and cast at the read:

l_out: str
l_lat: float
if lora_model:
    l_out, l_lat, l_tps, l_vram = generate_response(lora_model, prompt)
    ...
else:
    bprev = base_evals[idx - 1]
    l_out = cast(str, bprev["out"])
    l_lat = cast(float, bprev["latency"])

This is the pattern used in deep_multi_experiment_suite.py and enterprise_production_eval_suite.py.

docs.title: Adding a New Module
docs.text:
1. Write it strict from the start (annotate every function signature).
  2. Add the path to both lists: Makefile (typecheck-strict) and .pre-commit-config.yaml (mypy-strict hook args).
  3. Run make typecheck-strict — must pass with the new module included.
  4. If the module needs a lazy third-party import, import it under if TYPE_CHECKING: for annotations and keep the runtime import local (see ricc/observability/__init__.py).

docs.title: Analytics & Reports
docs.text: ricc/analytics/ computes the statistical and semantic profile of the corpus and renders it into reports consumed by the CLI, the Streamlit Studio and the docs pipeline.

docs.title: Engine
docs.text:
DeepChatAnalyzer (engine.py, ~700 LoC, strict-typed) computes:

  • Message metrics — length distributions (chars/words/token estimates with percentiles), activity by hour/year, inter-arrival times.
  • Author metrics — messages per author, participation concentration.
  • Social network analytics — via ricc/analytics/network.py (reply-graph degree/centrality).
  • Topic clustering — TF-IDF + clustering over tagged messages, surfaced as topic groups.
  • Longitudinal trends — per-domain volume evolution.

Metric definitions shared with docs/reports live in ricc/analytics/metrics.py; ReportGenerator (ricc/analytics/report_generator.py) renders the JSON report consumed by cli.py analyze and the Studio's tech-radar page.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• reports/analytics_summary.json — the full analysis payload.
  • Markdown reports rendered from JSON sources (single source of truth — the tests/test_metrics_consistency.py guard fails the build if a published figure drifts from the manifest).

docs.title: Where to Look
docs.text:
• CLI: make analyze / python cli.py analyze --limit 100000.
  • Studio: "Технологический радар" page renders hourly/yearly activity and top slang terms from the same JSON.

docs.title: Performance Notes
docs.text: The analyzer samples NLP-heavy paths (--limit); full-corpus runs are only needed when regenerating release reports (make reports-real). Percentile helpers are pure functions unit-tested in tests/test_analytics_engine.py.

docs.title: Deduplication
docs.text: ricc/deduplication/ removes duplicate and near-duplicate messages before taxonomy tagging and export. Two stages, both strict-typed.

docs.title: Stage 1 — Exact Duplicates
docs.text:
ExactDeduplicator (exact_dedup.py):

  • Normalizes text (whitespace, unicode NFC) and hashes with xxHash (XXH3) and SHA-256 for provenance.
  • O(n) set lookups; the hash of every kept message is recorded in the artifact manifest (reports/dataset_manifest.json) so downstream consumers can verify corpus identity.

docs.title: Stage 2 — Near Duplicates (MinHash LSH)
docs.text:
MinHashLSH (minhash_lsh.py):

  • Shingles the normalized text into character n-grams.
  • MinHash signature (configurable permutations) + LSH banding for candidate pairs — sublinear in corpus size.
  • Jaccard similarity above the threshold marks a near-duplicate cluster; the lexicographically-first message id is kept as the canonical one.

docs.title: Why Both
docs.text: Exact hashing is cheap and catches copy-paste/fwd spam; MinHash catches reposts with edited punctuation, trailing quotes or emoji. Both stages record removed counts into the pipeline log (stage_end(removed=...)) and the messages counter (ricc_pipeline_messages_processed_total).

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text: Thresholds and shingle size are module constants in minhash_lsh.py — they are conservative by default. If you observe false merges on short technical messages (e.g. +1, ok), raise the min-length floor before touching the similarity threshold, and re-run make validate.

docs.title: Downstream Effects
docs.text:
• Removed messages never reach full_clean_messages.parquet.
  • Dedup statistics feed the analytics report and the dataset manifest.

docs.title: Drift Monitoring — PSI, Jensen-Shannon, Vocabulary Jaccard
docs.text: ricc/monitoring/drift.py (DatasetDriftMonitor) compares a reference dataset snapshot against the current one and quantifies drift with three standard metrics. Thresholds live in params.yaml (single source of truth).

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Metric Stable Moderate Significant Detects PSI (message-length distribution) < 0.10 0.10–0.25 > 0.25 general distribution shift JS divergence (bits, domain shares) < 0.05 0.05–0.20 > 0.20 topical shifts (community changing focus) Vocab Jaccard (top-500 tokens) > 0.90 0.75–0.90 < 0.75 lexical drift in corpus language

Overall verdict: significant_drift if any metric is significant, else moderate_drift if any is moderate, else stable.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
# Self-comparison baseline (reference == current) => stable
python scripts/run_drift_monitoring.py

# Real temporal drift: point at two frozen snapshots
python scripts/run_drift_monitoring.py \
    --reference dataset_output/parquet/full_clean_messages_2026Q2.parquet \
    --current   dataset_output/parquet/full_clean_messages.parquet

The script writes reports/drift_report.json and prints the verdict.

docs.title: Interpreting the Report
docs.text:
{
  "overall_verdict": "moderate_drift",
  "metrics": {
    "length_psi":       {"value": 0.12, "verdict": "moderate_drift"},
    "domain_distribution": {"js_divergence_bits": 0.03, "verdict": "stable",
                            "biggest_share_shift_domain": "ai_ml_nlp",
                            "biggest_share_shift_pp": 1.7},
    "vocabulary":       {"jaccard_overlap": 0.93, "verdict": "stable",
                         "new_top_tokens": 31, "dropped_top_tokens": 27}
  },
  "thresholds": {"psi": {"stable": 0.1, "moderate": 0.25}, "...": "..."}
}
  • biggest_share_shift_pp names the domain that moved the most (percentage points) — start the investigation there.
  • A self-comparison baseline on two random subsamples of the same corpus can show moderate vocabulary drift from sampling noise alone. That is informational: the SLO gate treats moderate_drift as non-blocking and blocks only on significant_drift.

Gauge Meaning ricc_drift_psi_value latest PSI ricc_drift_js_value latest JS divergence (bits) ricc_drift_vocab_jaccard latest vocab overlap ricc_drift_verdict_total{verdict} per-metric and overall verdict counters

The Grafana panel "Drift metrics" plots the three gauges; the alert RiccDriftSignificant fires on any significant_drift verdict.
