docs.title: Export Formats
docs.text: ricc/exporter/ turns cleaned messages, SFT dialogues, RAG chunks and DPO pairs into training-ready files. All exporters are strict-typed and covered by round-trip tests (tests/test_exporters_roundtrip.py).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
File Exporter Format dataset_output/parquet/full_clean_messages.parquet ParquetExporter columnar corpus (canonical artifact) dataset_output/parquet/sft_dialogues.parquet ParquetExporter SFT dialogue table dataset_output/parquet/rag_knowledge_base.parquet ParquetExporter RAG chunk table dataset_output/jsonl/sft_openai_messages.jsonl JSONLExporter OpenAI ChatML {"messages": [...]} dataset_output/jsonl/sft_sharegpt.jsonl JSONLExporter ShareGPT conversations dataset_output/jsonl/sft_alpaca.jsonl JSONLExporter Alpaca instruction/input/output dataset_output/jsonl/rag_knowledge_base.jsonl RAGExporter chunk records with metadata dataset_output/jsonl/dpo_preference_pairs.jsonl DPOExporter chosen/rejected pairs

The three parquet files are the canonical artifacts: the dataset manifest (reports/dataset_manifest.json) pins their sha256 digests, and the SLO gate verifies provenance against it.

docs.title: The contract is versioned
docs.text:
The column set of these files is the public contract of the project. It is declared in ricc/schema_version.py — the column names, their order and their Arrow types — and:

  • every exported Parquet file carries the contract version and fingerprint in its Arrow metadata, so a downloaded file says which contract it was written against;
  • the validator enforces it: a renamed, reordered or retyped column fails the validation instead of passing silently;
  • reports/dataset_schema.json records the whole contract, and CI keeps it in sync with the code.

See ADR 0006.

docs.title: The export streams
docs.text:
ParquetExporter writes through a pyarrow.parquet.ParquetWriter in batches, so the peak memory is bounded by the row group rather than growing with the corpus, and the file has many row groups (29 instead of 3 for the message corpus) — a consumer can read a slice instead of decompressing a third of the file.

Three properties the streaming writer guarantees:

  • the schema is pinned (MESSAGE_SCHEMA / SFT_SCHEMA / RAG_SCHEMA), because inferring it from the first batch alone is unsafe: a first batch whose reply_to_id is all-None yields a null column and a later batch with real integers then fails outright;
  • the write is atomic (a .partial file plus os.replace), so a failed export never leaves a truncated file where a consumer expects a dataset;
  • a later batch with a different key set is aligned to the schema (missing key → null, unknown key → dropped and logged) instead of producing a corrupt file. strict_schema=True turns the alignment into an error.

The file grows ~7 % compared to the single-shot writer: zstd compresses a large block better than a small one. The extra bytes buy the ability to read a slice.

docs.title: ChatML Masking
docs.text: SFT exporters apply prompt-loss masking (-100 over the prompt tokens) as a training-time transform in the LoRA loaders — the JSONL stores the raw dialogue, masking happens in LoRA Training.

docs.title: Provenance & Sync
docs.text: ricc/exporter/finalize_sync_all.py is the release-side finisher: verifies the artifact manifest, reconciles local artifacts with the pinned Hugging Face Hub revision, uploads the adapters that satisfy the training policy, and regenerates reports/LORA_MODEL_ZOO.md. It fails closed: an upload error aborts the release instead of being swallowed with a warning.

docs.title: Regenerating Reports
docs.text:
make reports       # model zoo catalog
make reports-real  # JSON reports from REAL local parquet (CI-fresh stats)

reports-real refuses synthetic markers — it is the honest-numbers path.

docs.title: Graph Extraction — Conversation Threads
docs.text: ricc/graph/ reconstructs the reply structure of Telegram group chats into a thread DAG, which is what makes SFT dialogue extraction and RAG chunking possible.

docs.title: Thread DAG Builder
docs.text:
ThreadDAGBuilder (thread_builder.py):

  • Links messages by reply_to_id; messages without a reply target start a new thread root.
  • Handles Telegram quirks: replies to deleted messages, forwarded chains, and edited timestamps.
  • Output: threads: dict[thread_id, list[CleanedMessage]] ordered by unixtime.

docs.title: Conversation Extractor
docs.text:
ConversationExtractor (conversation_extractor.py) walks each DAG and emits:

  • SFT dialogues — user/assistant-shaped multi-turn exchanges (question → answer(s)), later filtered by the SFT quality monitor before export.
  • RAG knowledge chunks — self-contained technical segments with a title, domain and date range (RAGChunk).

Both feed the export stage (Export Formats).

docs.title: Quality Gate
docs.text:
ricc/monitoring/sft_quality.py scores extracted dialogues on five sub-metrics — empty-response ratio, median assistant turn length, role balance, Russian-language ratio, duplicate-turn ratio — and fails the build when a floor is crossed. Run it standalone:

python -m ricc.monitoring.sft_quality --input dataset_output/parquet/sft_dialogues.parquet

The report lands in reports/sft_quality_report.json and is consumed by the SLO gate when present.

docs.title: Design Notes
docs.text:
• Threads are rebuilt from scratch on every pipeline run — no incremental state; the raw exports are the only source of truth.
  • The extractor is strict-typed and covered by unit tests including deleted-message and forwarding edge cases (tests/test_conversation_extractor.py, tests/test_thread_builder.py).

docs.title: LoRA Training
docs.text: ricc/lora/ fine-tunes domain adapters on the RICC corpus, sized for a single RTX 3060 (12GB) and scaled up to a multi-model zoo.

docs.title: Entry Points
docs.text:
Script Purpose batch_train_zoo.py the trainer: 61-model zoo, full-corpus SFT, 4-bit QLoRA for the 7–8B flagships, resumable checkpoints, provenance, auto-upload to wwewtech/russian-it-community-lora 
# one adapter
python -m ricc.lora.batch_train_zoo --only qwen2.5_1.5b_instruct --profile full

# a smoke test (15 steps, 400 dialogues) — NOT publishable
python -m ricc.lora.batch_train_zoo --only qwen2.5_1.5b_instruct --profile pilot

One trainer, not four. The zoo used to be four scripts with four copies of the same training loop: train_lora.py, train_20_popular_models.py, train_heavyweight_5_sota.py and batch_train_zoo.py (~130 duplicated lines of model loading, LoRA wrapping, tokenisation and TrainingArguments). The 4-bit QLoRA path lived only in the two legacy scripts, so the flagship 7–8B adapters could not be retrained by the zoo trainer at all — and train_lora.py had no resume, no held-out tail, no eval split and no training_meta.json, so it could not produce a policy-compliant adapter even in principle. The capability is now a flag on the one trainer (load_in_4bit), the zoo covers every adapter in lora_adapters/, and the three legacy scripts are gone.

The training policy is binding. AGENTS.md requires a real run to cover the whole corpus for at least one complete epoch. The policy_gate decides what may be published; see ADR 0005. A partial or time-boxed run is labelled PARTIAL and is never uploaded.

docs.title: Training Details
docs.text:
• Prompt-loss masking: -100 over prompt tokens so CrossEntropyLoss covers only assistant responses (all loaders).
  • VRAM: PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True set by setup_runtime_env(pytorch_alloc_conf=True); fp16 on CUDA, fp32 fallback on CPU.
  • Full corpus: the trainer uses the whole JSONL (a silent 1000-row truncation was removed — see the module docstring); use --samples for smoke runs.
  • LoRA config: r=16/α=32 for every run; target modules auto-detected (detect_target_modules handles GPT2/OPT/Falcon naming variants).
  • 4-bit QLoRA: the 7–8B flagships are quantized to NF4 so they fit on a 12 GB consumer card (load_in_4bit in the zoo definition).

docs.title: What may be published
docs.text:
ricc/lora/policy_gate.py is the single source of truth:

Requirement Why a training_meta.json exists without it there is no record of what was trained actual_steps ≥ one full epoch of the trainable set the corpus is covered, not a sample of it the run was not time-boxed a --hours budget stops the run early by definition the coverage is measured against the trainable set the held-out tail is never trained on

The gate runs in the trainer (before the Hub upload), in the release pipeline (finalize_sync_all skips non-compliant adapters) and in the registry generator (which records policy_compliant and the coverage). CI publishes the state of the whole zoo as reports/lora_policy_compliance.json.

The currently published zoo is entirely non-compliant (0 of 56): the seven adapters with metadata cover 16.5–44.6 % of the corpus and the other 49 are pilot checkpoints without provenance. Retraining them is a GPU job (~25 h for a 3B model, ~13 h for 1.5B, ~5–7 h below 1B on the RTX 3060), not a code change.

The canonical command for one adapter is derived from the dataset, not written down by hand:

python -m ricc.lora.batch_train_zoo --only <adapter_id> --profile full \
    --samples 200000 --steps 21420 --eval-frac 0.005 --holdout-tail 1000 \
    --seed 42 --keep-checkpoints --no-upload

21420 is ceil(171354 / 8) — one epoch over the trainable set of the current corpus. python -c "from ricc.lora.policy_gate import canonical_full_run; print(canonical_full_run(173216))" prints the current value.

docs.title: Continuing a long run
docs.text:
A full run takes hours, so it must be resumable:

  • the checkpoints are the resume points, and --force keeps them (it deletes the finished adapter, not the checkpoints);
  • --save-total-limit (default 10) decides how many are kept — the previous limit of 2 deleted every resume point within a thousand steps;
  • a run that is interrupted simply re-issues the same command: the trainer picks the latest checkpoint and continues to the target step count.

So the practical loop is: run the command, and if it stops (crash, power cut, Ctrl-C), run the same command again.

docs.title: Observability (12.2.0+)
docs.text:
Every run records its outcome:

  • success → record_lora_result() with duration, final train loss, steps and peak VRAM (ricc_lora_train_loss, ricc_lora_vram_usage_bytes, ricc_lora_train_duration_seconds, ricc_lora_train_total{status="success"}).
  • failure → the exception is classified via the GPU/ML taxonomy (record_classified_ml_error) and recorded with ricc_lora_train_total{status="failure"}; OOM vs adapter corruption is visible in ricc_errors_total{component}.

Grafana panels "Training loss by adapter" and "VRAM usage by adapter" plot the gauges; the RiccLoraTrainFailing alert fires on failures.

docs.title: Model Zoo
docs.text: reports/LORA_MODEL_ZOO.md and reports/lora_zoo_index.json catalog the trained adapters; make reports regenerates the catalog from local + Hub state. Release-side sync (finalize + upload + catalog) runs in the release workflow via ricc.exporter.finalize_sync_all. The registry carries the training provenance, so a policy-compliant adapter is distinguishable from a legacy one.

docs.title: Provenance & Retraining (prompt-masking rollout)
docs.text:
An adapter carries training_meta.json (with prompt_masking: true, final loss, steps, seed, LoRA config) only if it was trained with the fixed prompt-masked objective. Adapters without that file predate the 2026-10-17 masking fix — their loss included user-prompt tokens — and should be retrained:

# validate the fixed objective on one adapter, without touching the repo
python -m ricc.lora.batch_train_zoo --only qwen2.5_1.5b_instruct \
    --steps 15 --output-dir /tmp/lora_smoke --no-upload --no-report

# full zoo rollout: retrain every existing adapter in place
python -m ricc.lora.batch_train_zoo --force --steps 15

Useful batch_train_zoo.py flags: --only <ids> (comma-separated filter), --output-dir, --no-upload, --no-report (legacy alias --no-catalogs) to skip the run report, --force (retrain adapters that already exist).

docs.title: Full-corpus & night runs
docs.text:
batch_train_zoo.py --profile full runs one complete epoch over the whole corpus: the step count is derived from the dataset size, the sample cap is the corpus, there is a 2% eval holdout on top of the 1 000-dialogue held-out tail, step-level training_log.jsonl, automatic checkpoints with resume from checkpoint-*, and a v2 training_meta.json (actual_steps, required_steps_for_full_epoch, corpus_coverage_pct, train_dialogues, dataset_sha256, tok/s, peak VRAM). The aggregate run report goes to reports/lora_zoo_training_run.json + reports/LORA_ZOO_TRAINING_REPORT.md and never overwrites the canonical catalog.

For long unattended runs use wall-clock budgets. --hours N stops training gracefully after N hours (saving the adapter, and with --keep-checkpoints also resumable checkpoints); --holdout-tail N excludes the last N dialogues from training so the same dialogues stay clean for honest post-training benchmarks. A time-boxed run is a partial run: it is recorded as PARTIAL and is not published.

python -m ricc.lora.batch_train_zoo --only phi_3.5_mini_instruct \
    --profile full --hours 5 --holdout-tail 1000 --keep-checkpoints --no-upload

scripts/run_lora_benchmark.py then measures base vs adapter on that tail (full-sequence perplexity + greedy generation snapshots; add --lm-eval-tasks humaneval after pip install lm-eval):

python scripts/run_lora_benchmark.py --adapter lora_adapters/phi_3.5_mini_instruct

The one-command overnight flow chains time-boxed training for several models with those benchmarks and writes reports/LORA_NIGHT_RUN_SUMMARY.md:

python scripts/night_run_full_corpus.py --total-hours 10 \
    --models phi_3.5_mini_instruct qwen2.5_1.5b_instruct --split-weights "60,40"

A 10-hour night is only a partial epoch on a 3.8B model — each adapter records the honest fraction of the corpus it actually saw as corpus_coverage_pct in training_meta.json, and the policy gate refuses to publish it.

docs.title: PII Anonymization
docs.text: RICC's core guarantee is Zero-PII: no phone numbers, emails, crypto wallets, API keys or real names survive into the published dataset.

docs.title: Two-Layer Scrubbing
docs.text:
UnifiedPIIAnonymizer (ricc/pii/anonymizer.py) chains:

  1. Regex layer (ricc/pii/regex_scrubber.py) — deterministic masks for phone numbers (RU/international formats), emails, crypto wallets (TRC20/ERC20/BTC), OpenAI-style API keys.
  2. NER layer (ricc/pii/ner_scrubber.py) — Natasha/Slovnet person-name detection with morphological declension handling (ricc/pii/deep_anonymizer.py extends it with name-form dictionaries).

Layer 2 runs after layer 1, so the NER model never sees literal contact strings, only prose.

docs.title: Pseudonymization
docs.text: Authors are replaced with stable anonymous IDs (author_anon / author_id_anon); the mapping never leaves the pipeline. Community node names are treated as quasi-identifiers and normalized.

docs.title: Audits
docs.text:
Command What it does make audit red-team adversarial audit (RedTeamPIIAuditor) on the full corpus make audit-prob stratified probabilistic audit: sample + Wilson CI (99%) + power analysis cli.py audit-prob --sample-size 50000 --confidence 0.99 parameterized run

The probabilistic audit is the release-blocking proof: a leak rate above max_leak_tolerance (default 1e-4) fails the SLO gate.

docs.title: Metrics & Reports
docs.text:
• Findings per category → ricc_pii_audit_leaks_found_total{category}.
  • Verdict → ricc_pii_audit_verdict_total{verdict=PASSED|LEAKS_DETECTED}.
  • Reports: reports/pii_validation_report.json, reports/probabilistic_pii_audit.json.
  • Any LEAKS_DETECTED fires a critical alert (RiccPiiLeaksDetected) in the monitoring stack.

docs.title: Interactive Sandbox
docs.text: The Streamlit Studio has a live scrubber page (Zero-PII песочница) where you can paste text and see every masked entity — useful for testing the scrubber against new PII formats before adding them to the regex layer.

docs.title: Adding a New Pattern
docs.text:
1. Add the regex to ricc/pii/regex_scrubber.py (with a unit test).
  2. Add a red-team case to ricc/validation/pii_redteam.py.
  3. Re-run make audit and make audit-prob.

docs.title: Quality Gates
docs.text: The platform ships the mechanisms that make its claims checkable. Every one of them fails closed: a gate that cannot verify a thing reports a failure, not a pass.

docs.title: The gates
docs.text: Gate What it proves Where Fails closed on Probabilistic PII audit The 99 % upper bound on the message-level leak rate stays below the tolerance, over 12 categories ricc/validation/probabilistic_audit.py a corpus it cannot read; a category it does not cover Training policy gate A published adapter covered a full epoch of the corpus and was not time-boxed ricc/lora/policy_gate.py missing provenance; a partial epoch SLO gate Validation, PII audit, drift, SFT quality and artifact provenance all pass before a release ricc/monitoring/slo_gate.py a missing report; a synthetic fixture Artifact manifest The published Parquet files are byte-identical to the snapshot that was audited ricc/validation/artifact_manifest.py a hash mismatch Dataset contract The column names, order and types match the declared contract, and the version metadata is current ricc/schema_version.py a renamed, reordered or retyped column SFT quality monitor The real corpus (not a fixture) meets the dialogue-quality floors ricc/monitoring/sft_quality.py a corpus it could not read DVC lock The pipeline can be reproduced from the pinned raw exports dvc.lock, dvc.yaml a stage whose inputs changed

docs.title: Why they fail closed
docs.text:
A gate that passes when it cannot check anything is worse than no gate: it converts an unknown into a green light. The concrete cases this project hit:

  • The PII audit reported PASSED on a corpus whose text_clean column did not exist — every row became an empty string, so zero leaks were "found" and the report carried a 99 % confidence statement about a corpus it had never read.
  • The sft_quality monitor reported a hard FAIL on the real corpus (it parsed zero of 171 520 dialogues, because the parquet stores list<struct> and the monitor only understood lists and JSON strings) while the synthetic CI fixture passed — the gate was validating the fixture.
  • The artifact_manifest verification in CI compared a manifest that had just been created from the same files, so it could never fail.

All three now refuse to certify what they cannot verify.

docs.title: Running them
docs.text:
# the privacy proof
python scripts/run_probabilistic_pii_audit.py

# the training policy, for the whole zoo
python -c "from pathlib import Path; from ricc.lora.policy_gate import evaluate_compliance; \
[print(p.name, evaluate_compliance(p).compliant) for p in sorted(Path('lora_adapters').iterdir()) if p.is_dir()]"

# the dataset contract
python scripts/generate_schema_manifest.py --check

# the release verdict
python -m ricc.monitoring.slo_gate --json-out reports/slo_verdict.json

docs.title: In CI
docs.text: Job Gate test the unit and integration suite, with the coverage floor coverage-regression the changed lines must be covered (diff-cover) validate the dataset validation, the PII audit and the reconciliation dvc-consistency the raw-export dependency list, the stage definitions and the lock file slo-gate / slo-gate-real the release verdict, on synthetic and on the real corpus security bandit, detect-secrets and pip-audit

docs.title: The statistical honesty of the benchmarks
docs.text:
The evaluation suites compare variants that run on the same tasks, so the comparison is paired and McNemar's exact test applies. On the published raw outputs no comparison is significant (p ≥ 0.125), and the report says so instead of claiming an improvement. The benchmark suites also refuse to run without the adapter rather than writing the base results into the LoRA column — that fallback is what produced the previously retracted numbers.

See ADR 0003, ADR 0005 and ADR 0006.

docs.title: RAG Pipeline
docs.text: ricc/rag/rag_pipeline.py (LocalRAGPipeline) is a dependency-light hybrid retrieval engine over the 325k-chunk knowledge base: CPU-only, built on scikit-learn (already a core dependency).

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
query ──> Stage 1: lexical str.contains pre-filter (cap 5000)
      ──> Stage 2: per-query TF-IDF (1-2 grams, 20k features) + cosine re-rank
      ──> hybrid score = 0.65·tfidf + 0.35·lexical (scaled 0..10)
  • Per-query TF-IDF fit keeps memory flat: no global 325k×30k matrix; the vectorizer is fitted on the candidate set plus the query.
  • Graceful degradation: without sklearn, or with < 2 candidates, the pipeline falls back to lexical scores — search() never raises on retrieval errors, it returns [].
  • mode="hybrid" (default) | "lexical" | "tfidf".

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from ricc.rag.rag_pipeline import LocalRAGPipeline

kb = LocalRAGPipeline(Path("dataset_output/parquet/rag_knowledge_base.parquet"))
hits = kb.search("как настроить nginx reverse proxy", top_k=3, domain_filter="devops_infra")
# hits: [{"chunk_id", "title", "domain", "tags", "content", "date_range", "score"}, ...]

prompt = kb.format_rag_prompt("вопрос", hits)  # context-augmented LLM prompt

docs.title: Consumers
docs.text:
• ricc/inference.py — terminal chat (cli.py chat), injects top-k context into the system prompt.
  • official_academic_benchmarks.py — RAG-augmented benchmark variants (HumanEval / RuMMLU with retrieved context).
  • Streamlit Studio — "База знаний RAG" search page.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text: tests/test_rag_pipeline.py covers ranking order (hybrid > lexical on domain-targeted queries), domain filtering, empty-KB and missing-sklearn fallbacks, and the BenchmarkComparator keyword-recall metric.

docs.title: Full Run
docs.text:
make run          # = python main.py
# or
python cli.py run # same stages, with --skip-ner option

The pipeline (ricc/pipeline.py, MasterDataPipeline) executes 7 stages in order, each timed and recorded into Prometheus (ricc_pipeline_stage_total, ricc_pipeline_stage_duration_seconds):

  1. Ingestion — merge raw Telegram exports (ChatExport_* dirs).
  2. PII anonymization — UnifiedPIIAnonymizer (regex + Natasha NER).
  3. Deduplication — exact hash + MinHash LSH.
  4. Taxonomy tagging — 9 IT domains, Aho-Corasick keywords.
  5. Graph extraction — thread DAG reconstruction.
  6. Export — Parquet / JSONL (ShareGPT, Alpaca, ChatML, RAG, DPO).
  7. Analytics & validation — statistical report + dataset validation.

Raw exports are configured in ricc/settings.py (RAW_EXPORT_DIRS); outputs land in dataset_output/ (parquet/, jsonl/), reports in reports/.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11–3.14, dependencies installed (make install).
  • Natasha NER downloads its models on first run into .hf_cache/ (set HF_HOME or let the bootstrap point it at the repo-local cache).
  • Input data: place Telegram result.json exports under the configured RAW_EXPORT_DIRS.

docs.title: Useful Commands
docs.text:
make analyze   # statistical/semantic report on exports
make validate  # schema + zero-PII audit
make slo       # SHIP/HOLD release verdict from reports/
make reports-real  # regenerate JSON reports from REAL parquet

docs.title: Orchestration
docs.text:
Prefect is optional (pip install .[platform]):

make orchestrate   # run the Prefect flow (graceful fallback without it)
make dvc-repro     # reproduce the DVC pipeline

Without Prefect the flow degrades to sequential execution.

docs.title: Metrics During a Run
docs.text: If the Streamlit app or another process started the metrics server, stage counters/durations are live on http://localhost:9090/metrics and in the Grafana observability profile.

docs.title: After the Run
docs.text:
1. make validate — confirm zero-PII and schema checks pass.
  2. make slo — release verdict; HOLD means a data-quality check failed (see reports/slo_verdict.json for the failing check names).
  3. Drift monitoring — compare against a frozen reference snapshot before releasing.

docs.title: SLO Gate — SHIP/HOLD Release Verdict
docs.text:
ricc/monitoring/slo_gate.py aggregates all quality signals into one release verdict. Exit code 0 = SHIP, 1 = HOLD; missing proof is fail-closed for privacy signals.

make slo   # = python -m ricc.monitoring.slo_gate --json-out reports/slo_verdict.json

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: Check Source Blocking Missing source validation reports/validation_results.json overall_passed yes HOLD pii-audit reports/probabilistic_pii_audit.json verdict yes HOLD (fail-closed) drift reports/drift_report.json overall_verdict only significant_drift; moderate_drift is informational (sampling noise) skip (warning) sft-quality reports/sft_quality_report.json when present skip pipeline-volume reports/pipeline_execution_stats.json cleaned > 0 yes skip artifact-manifest sha256 verify of canonical parquet against reports/dataset_manifest.json yes HOLD (fail-closed) hub-reconciliation reports/dataset_reconciliation_report.json status only on mismatch skip (warning)

docs.title: Synthetic-Smoke Guard
docs.text: CI builds 100-row synthetic fixtures for speed. Reports stamped _source.synthetic=true (reports/synthetic_fixture.json) are treated as SMOKE: the gate downgrades SHIP to HOLD with an explicit synthetic-smoke check, so a fake-data run can never green-light a release.

docs.title: Verdict Semantics
docs.text:
• SHIP — every blocking check passed on real artifacts.
  • HOLD — read reports/slo_verdict.json: checks[] lists each check with passed and a detail explaining the failure (e.g. manifest verify failed: digest mismatch for dataset_output/parquet/full_clean_messages.parquet).

docs.title: CI Integration
docs.text: The SLO Release Gate (Real Corpus) job runs the gate against real-corpus reports regenerated in CI; the release workflow gates publishing on it. The verdict counter ricc_slo_gate_verdict_total{verdict} feeds the RiccSloGateHold alert.

docs.title: Running in Tests
docs.text: evaluate(reports_dir) is a pure function returning a SloVerdict dataclass — tests/test_hybrid_rag_slo.py covers SHIP, HOLD and synthetic-smoke paths.

docs.title: Taxonomy & Tagging
docs.text: ricc/taxonomy/ assigns every message an IT domain and technical tags.

docs.title: Domains
docs.text:
Nine domains, keyword lists in params.yaml (domain_taxonomy: — single source of truth, consumed by TechnicalTagger via Aho-Corasick):

ai_ml_nlp, backend_databases, frontend_ui, devops_infra, business_legal_fintech, sysadmin_security, career_team_management, general_tech_chat.

Matching is case-insensitive with Russian keyword support; the classifier (ricc/taxonomy/classifier.py) combines keyword density with heuristics and falls back to general_tech_chat when confidence is low.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: TechnicalTagger (ricc/tagger.py) extracts technology tags (docker, kubernetes, postgres, lora, react, ...) from the same keyword tables. Tags are stored as a list column in the parquet exports and drive the RAG knowledge-base domain filter.

docs.title: Extending
docs.text:
1. Edit params.yaml — add keywords to an existing domain or a new domain block (the classifier picks it up automatically).
  2. python cli.py run re-runs tagging; or tag incrementally via the pipeline stage.
  3. Check domain balance: python cli.py analyze reports per-domain volumes; a heavily skewed distribution is normal for a technical community but feeds the drift monitor baseline.

docs.title: Where It Lands
docs.text:
• full_clean_messages.parquet — domain, tags columns.
  • rag_knowledge_base.parquet — topic_domain, topic_tags (used by LocalRAGPipeline.search(domain_filter=...)).
  • Analytics reports — per-domain volumes, trends and the tech radar.

docs.title: Validation & Audits
docs.text: ricc/validation/ is the quality police: schema checks, zero-PII proof, artifact integrity and Hub reconciliation. All checks feed the SLO gate.

docs.title: Dataset Validator
docs.text:
DatasetValidator (validator.py, make validate):

  • Parquet checks — the published contract is enforced: the column names, their order and their types must match the declaration in ricc/schema_version.py, and the file must carry the current contract version and fingerprint. A mismatch fails the validation with the status INVALID and a list of the problems.
  • JSONL checks — parseability, message schema (JSONLValidationError details the offending line).
  • SFT checks — role balance, non-empty assistant turns.
  • Aggregate result: reports/validation_results.json with overall_passed.

The contract itself is declared in ricc/schema_version.py, fingerprinted, and recorded in reports/dataset_schema.json (python scripts/generate_schema_manifest.py). See ADR 0006.

docs.title: Red-Team PII Audit
docs.text: RedTeamPIIAuditor (pii_redteam.py, make audit) adversarially searches the full corpus for PII patterns the scrubber might have missed — it is the "assume the anonymizer failed" counterpart of the pipeline's anonymization stage.

docs.title: Probabilistic Audit
docs.text:
scripts/run_probabilistic_pii_audit.py (also cli.py audit-prob): stratified sampling + Wilson CI (99%) + power analysis. This is the release-blocking zero-PII proof — a leak rate above tolerance fails the SLO gate. The parameters live in params.yaml (pii_audit:) and are read through settings.pii_audit; the CLI flags override them.

It fails closed. A corpus without the audited text_clean column is reported as FAILED_MISSING_COLUMNS, never as PASSED: an audit that cannot read the corpus must not certify it. The audit covers 12 leak categories — the seven the scrubber always checked, plus the secret assignments, private invite links, credentialed DB URLs, Telegram forward headers and raw user mentions it cleans but used to ignore.

The sample size has a statistical reason. With zero observed leaks the one-sided 99% upper bound is ~3.29/sample_size, so the sample must be large enough for that to stay under the tolerance: 50 000 gives 1.08e-04 (false LEAKS_DETECTED on a clean corpus), 100 000 gives 5.41e-05. The same maths works the other way: a small corpus cannot be certified at all (50 messages give an upper bound of 0.098).

The sampling is a genuine probability sample. Each stratum is drawn with its own RNG; using one random_state for all of them made the selection systematic — the same relative positions in every stratum — and the confidence interval invalid.

docs.title: Artifact Manifest
docs.text:
artifact_manifest.py pins canonical paths + sha256 digests:

python -m ricc.validation.artifact_manifest create --root . --manifest reports/dataset_manifest.json
python -m ricc.validation.artifact_manifest verify --root . --manifest reports/dataset_manifest.json

verify_manifest is used by the SLO gate (fail-closed: missing or stale manifest → HOLD). The module has hardening against path escape, symlink and partial-write attacks — see tests/test_artifact_manifest.py.

docs.title: Hub Reconciliation
docs.text: hub_reconciliation.py compares the local manifest against the pinned Hugging Face Hub revision snapshot (reports/pinned_hub_manifest.json). Statuses: EXACT_MATCH, DOCUMENTED_DIVERGENCE (acceptable, documented), or mismatch (fails the gate).
